findings.where: First screen: the h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu', with the coming-soon notice at the foot of the page (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The h1 promises a ranked list of hostels, but the page has no hostels. The first screen never says what MantaHostels is or that listings are not live yet. A visitor finds that out only at the very bottom, after reading the whole guide. The 5-second test fails on 'what is this and why should I care'. The h1 is also in title case, which breaks the brand's sentence-case voice.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who searched 'best hostels Canggu' and landed here. They expect hostels to compare and get a short essay instead, so the page feels like bait. That costs trust in a pre-launch brand that sells itself on honesty.

findings.where: Top of the page, desktop and phone: there is no hero band. Sand runs straight from the nav to the notice.
findings.fault: The brief says destination pages open with a loud top banner: a turquoise day ground, big type and illustration. This page has no top banner and no image or illustration of Canggu. The whole page is one quiet text document, the 'sterile' look the brand calls its enemy. The surf and beach destination gets no feeling at all.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand's spine (loud moments, calm machine) is missing. A backpacker gets a dry, wiki-like page with nothing that tells them what Canggu is like, where the brand promises personality and effortlessness.

findings.where: 'What to look for' section, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The brief names this as half of the page's job: what to look for in a hostel in Canggu. Yet it is the weakest heading on the page, a small uppercase eyebrow under the much larger 'Surf', 'Vibe' and 'Good for' headings. Its three-line paragraph reads like a footnote. When you squint, it loses to every other section.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker scanning on a phone for practical hostel advice. The one section meant for them reads as an afterthought and is easy to skip.

findings.fault: The list that answers 'does Canggu suit me?' is set in the smallest type on the page. It is twelve items run together in one dotted line, which on phone wraps over four ragged lines. It also covers nearly everyone: budget and couples, nightlife and yoga. The guide names no one Canggu doesn't suit, and no drawbacks such as traffic or crowds. A visitor can't use it to rule the place in or out.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker trying to judge fit. The key judgement is the hardest part to read, and an all-positive list reads like tourism promotion, not an honest guide.

findings.where: Desktop layout: the body column, the 'Good for' line and the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: The guide sits in a narrow left column with the right half of the screen empty. Two parts break that column: the 'Good for' line runs almost the full width, and the dark notice spans the full width while its text fills only the left half. The page has no consistent edge. The notice ends up as a large mostly-empty dark slab, the heaviest object on the page.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning the next hop. The page looks unfinished and lopsided, and the eye goes to the empty dark box instead of the guide.

findings.where: The guide's body as a whole, and the footer
findings.fault: The guide's claims (beginner-friendly breaks, boards within walking distance of most hostels) have no author, no 'last updated' date and no source. The footer has no year either. The site has no social proof (expected before launch, and it must not be invented), so nothing else on the page signals that the guide is current or that a real person checked it.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor weighing an unknown new site against Hostelworld's guides. With no date or named author, they can't tell whether the advice is current or written from first-hand knowledge.
